# v0.2.1

## Icons stop hiding what the device class knows

38 entities declared an icon although their device class already provides one.
For several of those, the device class provides a *state-dependent* icon: a
`plug` shows connected or disconnected, a `problem` shows alert or ok, a
`battery_charging` shows the charge state. A declared icon overrode all of
that with one static picture.

Icons are now declared only where no device class gives one — which means no
device class at all, or the `enum` device class, which has none of its own.
The register gate enforces the rule in both directions: an entity without a
device-class icon has to declare one, an entity with one must not.

The phase-switching pause sensor also had no display precision, so a whole
number of seconds could render with decimals.

## Hardware documentation

`docs/hardware.md` covers the part that happens before Home Assistant:

- cabling, the A/B/GND assignment and ordinary RS-485 practice —
  termination, topology, shielding, why the ground matters,
- the DIP switches: satellite mode on bank S1, the installation current on
  bank S2 DIP 6–8 with its value table, the §14a downgrade percentage on
  bank S2 DIP 4+5, and solar mode on DIP 7,
- the XG1 downgrade input, and the one question it decides — whether your
  §14a control box leaves you free to be the Modbus master,
- USB passthrough for Home Assistant OS, Supervised, Container and Core,
- reading the DIP-configured values back from the diagnostic sensors, so a
  wrong switch shows up as a number instead of as a mystery.

Every statement is marked as coming from the **Modbus specification** or from
the **installation manual**. Where a detail depends on a DIP numbering this
project cannot verify — which of DIP 6–8 is the most significant bit — it says
so rather than guessing, because getting that backwards would set 63 A where
16 A was meant. A repository check keeps the markers in place.

Entity ids, entity names and the device contract are unchanged.
